### Overview

In HackerRank, the duration a test remains active is determined by the expiration settings configured for that specific test or invitation. By default, the expiry option is set to 'Never', meaning the invitation does not expire unless manually configured otherwise.

### How Test Expiration Works

You can control test availability through the following methods:

1. **Test-Level Expiration**: You can define a specific start and end time (including time zone) for when a test remains active. Candidates can only attempt the test during this defined window.
2. **Invitation-Level Expiration**: When inviting candidates, you can set an expiry date via the 'Expiry' dropdown. If 'Custom' is selected, you can specify the exact date, time, and time zone.

### Important Considerations

- Once a test or invitation expires, invited candidates can no longer access the test.
- The 'Invite' button becomes disabled, and you cannot invite new candidates to an expired test.
- If a candidate is currently taking a test when the timer expires, the system will automatically submit the latest version of their code for scoring.

For more details on managing these settings, please refer to the official documentation: https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/6027855406-inviting-candidates-to-a-test

When should I create a variant versus
 have a different test?
detailed_results.expected_response:
Hi,


Consider these guidelines when choosing between creating a new test or a variant:



When to Use Test Variants:

Create variants to adapt a single test to different candidate profiles, 
such as roles with different tech stacks (React, Angular, Vue.js).
Variants streamline assessments by showing candidates only relevant sections and generating role-specific reports.


Advantages of Test Variants:

Reduces the need to manage multiple tests, improving efficiency.
Decreases maintenance while allowing scalable personalization.
Ensures candidates are tested on relevant content.


Disadvantages and Limitations of Test Variants:

A test must have at least two variants to function; you cannot delete a variant if only two exist.
Variants without logic are hidden from candidates until logic is added.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
### Overview

Test variants are designed to streamline your assessment process by allowing you to manage multiple tech stacks or role requirements within a single test setup. 

### When to Use Test Variants

Use test variants when you need to assess candidates on different tech stacks (e.g., Node.js, Python, or Java) or specific role requirements while maintaining a unified assessment structure. This approach is ideal for reducing maintenance overhead, as it allows you to manage one test rather than multiple separate ones.

### Advantages of Test Variants

- **Streamlined Management:** Reduces maintenance by consolidating multiple variations into a single test setup.
- **Candidate Experience:** Candidates see only the sections relevant to their specific input at login, and they receive helpful subtext to make informed decisions.
- **Clean Reporting:** Reports are specific to the variant attempted, ensuring insights remain role-specific and easy to evaluate.

### When to Create a New Test

Create a new, separate test when the assessment requirements are fundamentally different in scope, purpose, or structure, such that they do not share a common core or when you need to assess entirely different skill sets that do not fit within a single variant-based framework.

### Reference

- [Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/3121307537-july-2025-release-notes)
- [Create Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/7530103378)

detailed_results.predicted_response:
### Overview
To accommodate a candidate's request for extra time, you should apply the time extension directly within the HackerRank platform. If you also need to reinvite the candidate, please follow the separate steps for reinvitation.

### Adding Extra Time
1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account.
2. Go to the **Tests** tab and select the relevant test.
3. Navigate to the **Candidates** tab.
4. Select the checkbox next to the candidate.
5. Click **More > Add Time**.
6. Enter the additional minutes (e.g., 53) and click **Confirm**.

*Note: If the candidate is currently in a session, they must refresh their page to see the updated timer. If they have already completed the test, they will need to log in again to view the added time.*

### Reinviting a Candidate
1. In the **Candidates** tab of your test, select the checkbox next to the candidate.
2. Click **Invite selected**.
3. In the **Send Test Invites** section, click **Send invite**.
4. When the confirmation message appears, click **Re-invite**.
5. Click **Send invite** to complete the process.

### Reference
- [Adding extra time](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/4811403281-adding-extra-time-for-candidates)
- [Reinviting candidates](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/1002936098-reinviting-candidates-to-a-test)

Inviting candidates to a HackerRank test

1. Log in to your Recruitee account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Candidates** tab.

3. Select a candidate profile.

4. Click the more option menu and select **Send HackerRank test**.

5. In the **Send HackerRank test** dialog:

 - Review the candidate name and email address.

 - Select the **Test**, **Evaluator**, and **Job**.

After you send the test, the candidate profile displays a HackerRank badge.

Inviting candidates to a HackerRank interview

To invite candidates to a HackerRank interview:

After you schedule the interview, the candidate profile displays a HackerRank badge.

Inviting candidates to a HackerRank test

To invite candidates to a HackerRank test:

1. Log in to your Lever V2 admin account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Candidates** tab.

3. Select an existing candidate or or click **Add Candidate** to add a new candidate

 - If you select an existing candidate:

 1. Verify that the correct **Job** is selected.

Adding extra time

If your Visa card has been lost or stolen, you should take immediate action to secure your account.

#### Steps to Report
1. Visit the official Visa India [Lost or Stolen card page](https://www.visa.co.in/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html).
2. Use the resources provided on that page to report and block your card.
3. If you are traveling, you may also contact the Visa Global Customer Assistance Services (GCAS) for the specific country you are in to report the loss and request emergency services.

#### Notes
- You should also contact your issuing bank directly, as they manage your specific account and can provide immediate assistance with card cancellation and replacement.
- Keep a record of your card account number and the relevant emergency contact numbers in a safe place for future reference.

FAQ

### What should I do if my Visa card has been lost or stolen?

To report your Lost or Stolen Visa Card, please visit our [Lost or Stolen card](/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html) page. Our skilled support team can assist you at any time with reporting and blocking your Lost or Stolen card and look into providing you emergency services* if applicable.

### How can I find an ATM?

To find an ATM, please use Visa’s [ATM locator](https://www.visa.com/atmlocator/) to get currency at over 2 million ATMs worldwide.

### Security

### I was contacted by someone claiming to be from Visa. Is this real or a scam?

If you receive a call or email asking for your information, do not provide it. You can report a phone scam that uses Visa’s name by [contacting us](/contact-us.html). Visa does not call or email cardholders and request personal information.

### My identity has been stolen – what should I do?

Visit our [Lost or Stolen card](/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html) page – if the identity theft involves your Visa card – to learn how to cancel your card or get an emergency replacement card.

### Travel

### What do I need to know before I travel abroad?

Travel tips for every stage of your journey

### Get in touch with your bank

Check that your bank or credit card company has updated contact information. Tell them where and when you’ll be travelling – so that your card isn’t flagged for unusual activity.

### Know the emergency numbers for lost or stolen cards

Take note of your card account number and the telephone number for the Visa Global Customer Assistance Services (GCAS) of the country you are travelling to. Visa cardholders can report lost or stolen Visa cards and request emergency services by calling the GCAS number. Learn more about GCAS here.

Travel tips for every stage of your journey

### Activate your credit and debit cards before you travel

Check with your bank to confirm that your payment card has been activated for overseas travel use and take note of the daily ATM withdrawal limit for your card. Know the expiry dates, account balance and amount of credit available to you. This way, you won’t be caught short with a card that doesn’t work while you’re away, or not have enough credit to cover your trip expenses.

### Apply for mobile alerts

Sign up for free SMS transaction alerts to receive instant SMS messages when a transaction exceeds a pre-set amount or when unusual card activities are detected.

### Memorise your PIN

Whether you are using a magnetic strip or chip card, know your credit card PIN before travelling overseas. If you have forgotten your PIN, reapply for a new one.

### Make a copy of everything in your wallet

Keep a record of card account numbers and telephone numbers for reporting lost or stolen cards. But remember to keep this information in a safe place. Always keep your credit card number and the three-digit CVV2 code on the back of your Visa card confidential.
